segments.t: At a Parisian cafe terrace, Gabriel meets actress Virginie Efira while waiting for their director. When the director stands them up, Gabriel decides to reveal an uncomfortable truth about Mathias. Let's listen to the scene in French first.
Il ne vient pas?
Il est où, ton réalisateur?
Il nous a posé un lapin.
Comment ça se passe avec Mathias?
Si tu veux critiquer mon agent, laisse tomber.
De quoi il s'agit?
Tu mérites des gens de ton côté.
Bien sûr. Merci pour le café.
Je vais faire simple. Ramzy te ment.
Mathias aussi. Il te manipule.
Vous n'avez pas touché le même salaire.
Loin de là.
C'est pathétique.
J'ai lu le contrat de Ramzy.
Il y a un autre contrat secret.
Tu veux le voir?
Let's examine how Gabriel reveals Mathias's secret betrayal to Virginie.
Il ne vient pas?
'Is he not coming?' The key word here means 'is coming', paired with 'is coming' to make the point clear.
Il est où, ton réalisateur?
'Where is your director?' The adverb meaning 'where' sharpens the verb for 'is' here.
Il nous a posé un lapin.
'He stood us up.' An idiom meaning to stand someone up.
Comment ça se passe avec Mathias?
'How are things going with Mathias?' The verb meaning 'is going' anchors the whole remark.
Si tu veux critiquer mon agent, laisse tomber.
'If you want to criticize my agent, drop it.' Listen for the expression meaning 'want', which leads naturally into 'fall'.
De quoi il s'agit?
'What is this about?' Listen for the expression meaning 'is about', which leads naturally into 'is about'.
Tu mérites des gens de ton côté.
'You deserve people on your side.' Gabriel opens with the word for 'deserve' and lands on 'side' at the close.
Bien sûr. Merci pour le café.
'Of course. Thanks for the coffee.' A polite formula before leaving.
Je vais faire simple. Ramzy te ment.
'I will keep it simple. Ramzy is lying to you.' The key word here means 'am going to', paired with 'is lying' to make the point clear.
Mathias aussi. Il te manipule.
'Mathias too. He is manipulating you.' The short object word placed before the verb.
Vous n'avez pas touché le même salaire.
'You did not receive the same fee.' The key word here means 'did not have', paired with 'fee' to make the point clear.
Loin de là.
'Far from it.' Gabriel opens with the word for 'far' and lands on 'there' at the close.
C'est pathétique.
'This is pathetic.' An evaluative adjective expressing disbelief.
J'ai lu le contrat de Ramzy.
'I read Ramzy's contract.' Notice how the verb for 'I have' leads straight into 'contract'.
Il y a un autre contrat secret.
'There is another secret contract.' Gabriel opens with the word for 'is' and lands on 'secret' at the close.
Tu veux le voir?
'Do you want to see it?' The verb meaning 'want' anchors the whole remark. Now let's listen to the whole discussion again without stopping.
